question: Why do football clubs almost never disappear, even after going bankrupt?
answer: A club is worth more to its town than its accounts show. When one collapses, fans, local businesses and councils step in, a buyer takes the name and ground, and debts are cut. Kuper and Szymanski note that almost all English league clubs of the 1920s still exist. Badly run, rarely dead.
move: What people love gets rescued, so its failures are rarely punished.
ask: What do I keep rescuing out of loyalty, which never has to change because I always step in?
reference: Simon Kuper & Stefan Szymanski, Soccernomics, HarperSport, 2009
